producer_report.summary: The steward now calls a model. `steward::run` starts an agent through the shared driver, with the stored `STEWARD_PROMPT` (after the contract) as its system prompt. It works read-only in a per-run workspace that holds the visible code as a one-commit snapshot, a copy of `records/`, and `GIT-LOG.txt` (the last 200 commit subjects). The agent returns structured items. Athena validates each one: stable key alphabet, well-formed refs, cited jobs must exist, and an item on a rung the steward may change needs a request. Surviving items are deduped against recorded keys and sent through `decide()`. A rung at or below the limit queues a Request; a higher rung queues only a proposal with evidence. Blind-spot keys are `blind-spot:<source name>`, built by Athena, so error text never changes them. This covers GitHub unavailable, a source Athena could not write to the workspace, and unreadable records. The invocation is recorded as an `athena.invocation/1` with role `steward`. `Records` keeps it in `steward_runs`, so it never shows as a job. A run that queues nothing makes no commit; its invocation record waits in the state dir and goes in the next commit. A nested run does nothing. Root-cause fix for the earlier policy gap: the `gh` policy in `policy.rs` is now an allow-list. Any word starting `-f` or `-F` (including `-ftitle=x` and `-Fx=@f`), `--field`, `--raw-field`, `--input`, any method but GET (including `-XPOST`), graphql, headers and every unlisted flag are denied; mutating git and gh commands are denied. The old failure counting is kept as input to the agent's brief. Version 2 of the steward role records the model-backed prompt. To share the driver with the background thread, `AgentDriver` is now `Send + Sync` and `Athena.driver` is an `Arc`. Docs: `roles-and-ladder.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` say the steward calls a model and state the git-history, model/budget, GitHub-token and not-run-live limits. The requirements-map A9-1 row stays Partial with updated text.

checks_run.note: clean; one clippy type_complexity finding on the first run, fixed with a type alias
every target passes. Includes the 10 tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs and the 3 new gh policy tests. Live tests stay ignored.

open_issues: The model-backed steward has not run against the real Claude Code driver or hook. Tests use the fake driver, and the real `gh` allow-list is tested only as policy unit tests.

For `gh` to work in a live run, `GH_TOKEN` or similar must reach the agent through `[agents] env_pass_if_set` in `athena.toml`. I did not change `athena.toml`; without it the agent should report the `github` blind spot.
A run that queues nothing keeps its invocation record in `<state>/steward-pending` until a later run commits something, so the cost of empty runs is recorded late.
The steward borrows the verifier's model, cost cap and timeout, and is charged to no job; a steward-specific setting is future work (documented).
`GIT-LOG.txt` lists commit subjects from the user's real repository, so a subject naming a private path would be visible to the agent (documented).
A blind-spot item queues a Request, because blind spots sit on the Implementation rung and go through `decide()`. For a missing GitHub token that request cannot fix the cause.
mistakes: My first `gh` flag check let a value flag at the end of the command (`gh run list --limit`) pass. The new denied-forms test caught it, and it now needs a value.
My first nested test assumed the job would be rejected; a nested run lands it, which broke the test until I added `go_any`.

I did not touch `claude.rs`, `invocation.rs`, `scoring.rs`, `run.rs`, `outputs.rs` of other roles, or `invariant.rs`. Nothing in them needed a change to compile or pass, though they were listed as expected deliverables.
learnings: `Role` is matched exhaustively in test scripts (`common/mod.rs`, `retry.rs`, `run_pin_tests.rs`) and in `fake.rs::deterministic_turn`, so adding `Role::Steward` needed an arm in each.

`Athena.driver` was `Box<dyn AgentDriver>` and `AgentDriver` had no `Send + Sync` bound. The background steward needed `Arc` plus the bound. `Athena` itself is not `Send`, because capabilities are not, so the thread builds its own handle from git, state, driver, build and athena_bin.
`RecordSet::load` keeps the raw bytes of every file under `records/`, so the workspace copy needs no per-file git calls.
`Snapshot::create` hides `records/` and the athena-exclude paths, so the steward workspace adds `records/` from the record set after the snapshot.
A nested Athena in the cli tests lands a job whose README deletion would otherwise be rejected, so the nested test uses a `go_any` helper.
The Bash tool allows only cargo, chmod, git status|diff|log|show, ls, mv and rm, so edits had to go through Edit and Write.
desires: A way to run the real Claude Code driver in a throwaway check, to try the steward and its hook end to end.
Permission to run `grep` or `sed` through Bash, instead of Edit-only edits.
A Quantity accessor that is not `Option` for measured values.
